<reason>B more convincingly defended a bounded obligation using existing retail channels and explained why private break-even does not capture social value. A identified genuine labor costs and offered a credible disposal-charge alternative, but repeatedly asserted that reduced availability and higher prices would outweigh recovered food’s benefits. B answered enforcement pressure directly and acknowledged imperfect compliance. A’s final replies did not resolve the distinction between unprofitable recovery and socially wasteful recovery.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s challenge to counting lost full-price revenue as a social cost forced A to concede that the markdown itself is a transfer. B then correctly narrowed the remaining dispute to real handling costs and possible availability losses, exposing how much A’s negative balance depended on unestablished predictions.</best_rebuttal>
